A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, main sections, and appendices A–F. All 35 pages of each version support comparison of the text, tables, algorithms, and mathematical arguments.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, analytical regret bounds, and proofs, including in its appendices. Table 1 compares theoretical bounds; no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v2 remains a theoretical paper throughout its main text and appendices. It reports no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Procedures 4 and 6 change the adversarial-switch condition from Ei = 3log(T) to Ei ≥ 3log(T). This corrects the stopping behavior for noninteger thresholds. The sampling, elimination, probability-bank mechanism, and Appendix F extension are otherwise retained.

E1.justification: Neither version uses training or evaluation datasets or reports experimental test scenarios. Both analyze the same stochastic and adversarial delayed-bandit settings.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an empirical baseline evaluation. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparison methods, including Joulani et al. [2013] and Masoudian et al. [2024].

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols are present in either version. There are no changes to evaluation splits, metrics, budgets, sample sizes, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. Appendix F's algorithm modification and supporting theoretical analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. The correction to a concentration inequality concerns the theoretical analysis rather than statistical reporting of experiments.

E6.justification: The regret bounds in Table 1, Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, Corollary 5.4, and Appendix F are unchanged. No empirical numerical results or qualitative findings are added, removed, or revised.

T1.justification: Lemma C.3 restores a missing sum over t on the conditional-expectation side of its cumulative concentration bound. Theorem 5.1 also specifies that RALG is expressed in T, K, D, and possibly dmax and σmax. These are local mathematical corrections and qualifications; the main regret rates and proof structure remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims of near-optimal stochastic and adversarial regret from one delayed-feedback algorithm, including the factor-K improvement in the stochastic delay term over the cited prior bound.

C2.justification: The interpretations of average-gap delay dependence and the adaptive algorithm's advantages are retained. Section 6 preserves the same open questions about simpler optimal algorithms and more structured delays.

D1.justification: Algorithms 5 and 8 add explicit empty-set initialization for the processed-round sets indexed by sampling probability. This supplies previously omitted implementation detail for an existing mechanism. No code, data, or computing-resource disclosures change.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to SAPO and earlier delayed-bandit algorithms are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an initialization note to Procedure 4, clarifies the description of RALG, adjusts some algorithm-line references, and makes small capitalization and date edits. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Line numbers are added to Protocol 1 and Procedures 3, 6, 7, and 9. Algorithm blocks expand slightly, logarithm typesetting changes, and some equations and paragraphs move across page boundaries. The comparison and notation tables retain their structure; no figures are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 makes useful local repairs: the EAP threshold avoids an unreachable equality test for noninteger thresholds, Algorithms 5 and 8 explicitly initialize processed-round sets, and Lemma C.3 restores a missing summation. These improve the algorithm specification and mathematical precision while leaving the central contributions and regret guarantees unchanged.
